raw_response.overlap_rationale: Both Study A (Bond 2013, SAJHR) and Study B (Bond 2012, Third World Quarterly) are single-authored qualitative political-economy and legal-policy case-study essays by Patrick Bond rather than primary microdata surveys, and they have distinct overarching scopes: Study A critiques human-rights versus 'commons' advocacy narratives through the 2001-2009 Johannesburg/Soweto (Phiri) water commercialisation and Mazibuko v City of Johannesburg litigation alongside 2000-2012 global Climate Justice summits, whereas Study B traces urban township 'people power' across South Africa from the mid-1980s anti-apartheid civic movement (rent and bond boycotts, ACO, CAST, SANCO) to late-1990s/2000s struggles over Soweto electricity (SECC/Eskom disconnections and R1.4 billion arrears write-off), Orange Farm water meters, HIV treatment, and 2005-2011 Gatherings Act protests. However, for post-2000 municipal service delivery, both papers examine the same Johannesburg Free Basic Water tariff case (the 2001 6,000 litres/month free block with a steeply convex second block, Suez, APF, and 20,000 households/month disconnections) and cite the same underlying secondary empirical statistics (1.5 million people disconnected from water annually and the 1997/98-2004 Durban real water price doubling reducing consumption among the poorest third of residents), creating partial overlap in case-study and secondary empirical evidence.
raw_response.study_a_sample_and_data: Qualitative legal-political case study and secondary-data synthesis (no primary survey N) focused on Johannesburg and Phiri, Soweto (2001-2009), examining Suez's 2001-2006 Johannesburg Water management contract, Free Basic Water block tariffs (6 kl/month in 2001; 10 kl/month indigent policy in 2008), prepayment water meters, and the Mazibuko v City of Johannesburg litigation (2008 High Court, 2009 SCA, October 2009 Constitutional Court), supplemented by secondary figures on Durban tariff elasticity (1997-2004, Bailey & Buckley 2005), national water disconnections (1.5 million/year by 2003, Muller 2004), SAPS service delivery protests (2009-2012, >800/year), HSRC polls (2003-2011), and global Climate Justice conferences (2000-2012).
raw_response.study_b_sample_and_data: Macro-historical qualitative political-economy synthesis and secondary-data review (no primary survey N) of urban township social movements in South Africa from the mid-1980s to 2011 (centring on Soweto, Alexandra, Vaal, East Rand, Orange Farm, and Durban), covering 1984-1994 civic associations and rent/bond boycotts (~80 regional civics in 1990), post-1994 demobilisation, 2001-2003 Soweto Electricity Crisis Committee campaigns against Eskom disconnections (20,000 households/month; R1.4bn arrears cancelled in 2003), 2001-2003 Johannesburg/Orange Farm water tariff and prepaid meter conflicts, secondary statistics from Statistics SA (1995-2002), SALDRU (1993-2008), Bond & Dugard 2008 on Durban water consumption (1998-2004) and 1.5 million/year water disconnections, and Police Gatherings Act protest counts (>8,000/year since 2005).
